messages:
Marta B: hi folks, day 2 here — I can view the Notion onboarding templates but not edit. Also noticed there are region-specific copies (EU/NA/APAC). Where's the canonical source and how do we request edits without accidentally changing the regional versions?
Keon Y: welcome Marta! :wave: Canonical content lives in the master workspace 'Redwood Docs (Canonical)' > Templates > Onboarding. Regional copies are linked pages we sync from that canonical source.
Marta B: ah ok. I opened the EU copy and it says 'view only'. The button suggests requesting access but I'm not sure if that notifies Docs or the local owners.
Aria (Docs): Hey Marta : short path: we accept contributions through the docs-contrib PR flow so reviewers can confirm changes propagate safely to regional mirrors. If you need immediate edits for your team, duplicate the canonical template into your personal workspace, edit, then run the docs-bot submit flow.
Marta B: how do I find the canonical template? The regional copy doesn't clearly link back.
Keon Y: from the regional page click the small "Linked to" header (top right) — that shows the master page. Search also for the tag `#canonical` in the page header; canonical templates have that tag.
Taylor (IT): For edit permissions we use SSO groups. Quickest way is to fill the access form (Notion > Contributor): https://forms.redwood.internal/it-access and include your manager for approval. If it's an EU-specific legal wording change, tag the page with `#legal-review` so Docs Fellows get routed.
Marta B: Docs Fellows? what's that?
Aria (Docs): Docs Fellows are rotating reviewers from each org (prod, legal, eng) who triage incoming contributions. They help check tone, policy and region-specific compliance before we merge. When you invite docs-bot it creates a GH PR and pings the Fellows team.
Marta B: nice. If I duplicate and edit, does the bot preserve page properties and subpages?
Aria (Docs): Yes if you duplicate with subpages. The bot captures page content, properties, and most embeds. Figma/Loom embeds sometimes need manual re-linking. Images are included in the PR. The PR template asks for: short description, which regional mirrors to update, and whether it needs legal review.
Marta B: any naming conventions? I saw a few different styles across templates.
Keon Y: please use the prefix format: "[Dept] • Title" (that's a dot bullet to help sorting) and include a one-line summary under the title. Also add metadata at bottom: Owner, Reviewers, Last updated, Regions.
Marta B: got it. If I want to propose a new template (not editing canonical), still the same contrib flow?
Aria (Docs): yes, new templates still go through a PR so Fellows can check structure and search tags. For region-specific templates mark the PR with `regions: eu` etc.
Taylor (IT): FYI, IT can temporarily grant edit rights to a page owner for urgent changes. If you need that, include "urgent-edit" in the IT form note and your manager should approve.
Marta B: thanks — submitted the IT form and duplicated the canonical template. I'll invite docs-bot when ready.
Docs-bot: Thanks Marta! When you invite docs-bot@redwood please include a short PR note and the `regions:` field. Docs-bot will create a GitHub PR against docs-templates and tag the Docs Fellows.
Marta B: invited docs-bot and added PR note (minor wording and EU date formats). Thanks all for the quick help :heart:
Aria (Docs): Received the PR, will triage and loop in Legal if `#legal-review` is set. Welcome again!
Marta B: appreciate it — saved me a lot of time :)
